summary: AMD3 SET/GET/CLR OTA commands (per AIS-140 Amendment 3 Table 4D, $<IMEI>,<PASSWORD>,SET/GET/CLR,<cmd>:<val>*CS frame) sent via SMS or BLE were silently ignored - DecodeSMS() only understood the legacy ACTV/HCHK/+S*R textual commands and never checked for or routed the AMD3 frame, unlike TCP/RS232/RS485 which correctly route through DecodeOTAData()->ParseStandardAIS140Command().
root_cause: handleIncomingMessages() (Server.c) calls DecodeSMS(SMSData, OTA_SRC_SMS) for SMS and DecodeSMS(BTRcvBuffer, OTA_SRC_BLE) for BLE, but ProcessRS232OTAData()/ProcessRS485OTAData() and DecodeOTAData() (used by TCP sockets) all detect the '$'+IMEI AMD3 frame before falling back to DecodeSMS() for legacy commands. DecodeSMS() itself had no such detection, so AMD3 frames arriving via SMS/BLE fell through to the legacy parsers and were dropped.
fix: Added AMD3 frame detection at the top of DecodeSMS() (custom/SMS.c, under #ifdef PROTO_OG), mirroring the exact pattern already proven in DecodeOTAData() (Server.c:3763-3765): find '$', confirm NetWork.IMEI appears in the frame, call ParseStandardAIS140Command(frame, IsServer) and return. IsServer parameter already carries the correct OTA_SRC_* channel code (SMS=0, BLE=5) matching what ParseStandardAIS140Command expects.
evidence: Confirmed via full read of DecodeSMS (SMS.c:2051+), handleIncomingMessages (Server.c:5236+), ProcessRS232OTAData/ProcessRS485OTAData (SMS.c:3957+/4006+), and DecodeOTAData (Server.c:3752-3766) - RS232/RS485/TCP all check the '$'+IMEI pattern before falling back to DecodeSMS; DecodeSMS had zero such check anywhere in its ~1900 lines before this fix. Also confirmed handleCDACProtocol() (which does call DecodeOTAData(SMSData,0) for SMS) is PROTO_CDAC-only (guarded by #ifndef PROTO_CDAC / #else at Server.c:5586-5629) and never runs for PROTO_OG builds - ruling that out as an alternate SMS path for this product.
verification: Full `Make.bat new_release` GCC build succeeded (GCC Compiling Finished Successfully) with the fix in place; SMS.c compiled with no new warnings. Behavioral/on-device verification (actually sending an AMD3 SET/GET/CLR command via SMS to a live unit) NOT done - no hardware/SIM available this session.
must_not_repeat: When adding a new inbound command channel or reviewing SET/GET/CLR support, check that EVERY channel (TCP x2-4, SMS, BLE, RS232, RS485) independently detects the AMD3 '$'+IMEI frame before its legacy/fallback parser runs - grep for Ql_strstr(...,"$") is not enough, must confirm it precedes DecodeSMS()/legacy dispatch on that exact call path, since handleIncomingMessages vs handleCDACProtocol vs handleServerResponses are three separate, protocol-macro-gated dispatchers that each wire channels differently.

summary: OTA response SOURCE field (embedded in $PVT OTAResp, e.g. '(SCK1|SET|002:192.168.1.1:1)') sent a generic channel label (SCK1/SCK2/SMS/etc) for every source, but the AMD3 PDF's own worked examples require the actual originating address: server IP:port for a socket-received command, or the sender's phone number for SMS.
fix: Replaced the fixed src_str lookup with per-source formatting: OTA_SRC_SCK_1..4 now format VTSData.ServerData.IPn:Portn; OTA_SRC_SMS now uses the SMSSender global (populated from the SMS deliver URC's originating address in SMSLib.c before DecodeSMS/ParseStandardAIS140Command runs). BLE/RS232/RS485 keep a generic label since the spec's SOURCE examples only define IP:port and phone-number forms, not an RS232/RS485/BLE address.
evidence: PDF 'AIS-140 with Amd 3.pdf' OTA response section: '(device.vltsecurity.com:17234|SET|001:...:1)' and '(+91000000000|SET|002:...:1)' are the only two documented SOURCE forms, both concrete addresses, not channel labels.

related_finding_not_fixed: custom/Server.c MakeParamChangeString() (used by the LEGACY non-AMD3-frame command path via SendResponce(), e.g. 'SET:GIP'/'GET:APN' style commands) has the SAME class of bug PLUS its own: (1) it ignores its own Sender parameter via '(void)Sender;' and rebuilds a hardcoded label instead, and (2) its caller SendResponce() passes the wrong VTSData.ServerData index for OTA_SRC_SCK_2 (passes IP3 instead of IP2) and OTA_SRC_SCK_3 (passes IP4 instead of IP3), and has no case at all for OTA_SRC_SCK_4 (falls through to the BLE branch, wrongly triggering BLE_SendReply for a socket-4-sourced command). Not fixed this session - flagged to user as a separate, coupled bug requiring its own scoped fix (fixing MakeParamChangeString alone would just report a plausible-but-wrong IP for SCK_2/SCK_3 without also fixing SendResponce's indices).
must_not_repeat: When touching the OTA response SOURCE field, check BOTH producers: ParseStandardAIS140Command (AMD3 '$'+IMEI frame path, now fixed) and MakeParamChangeString/SendResponce (legacy 'SET:XXX' SMS-command-syntax path, still using generic labels + has its own IP-index bug) - they are two independent code paths feeding the same $PVT OTAResp field.

summary: Fixed the coupled bug flagged in the prior session: (1) MakeParamChangeString() ignored its own Sender parameter via '(void)Sender;' and always emitted a generic channel label (SCK1/SCK2/etc) into the $PVT OTAResp SOURCE field for legacy 'SET:XXX'/'GET:XXX'/'CLR:XXX' style SMS commands, instead of the spec-required IP:port or phone number. (2) Its caller SendResponce() passed the wrong VTSData.ServerData index for OTA_SRC_SCK_2 (passed IP3 instead of IP2) and OTA_SRC_SCK_3 (passed IP4 instead of IP3), and had no case at all for OTA_SRC_SCK_4 - which fell through to the final else branch and wrongly called BLE_SendReply() for a genuine socket-4-sourced command.
fix: MakeParamChangeString now builds SOURCE itself from the IsServer channel code (mirroring the earlier ParseStandardAIS140Command fix): OTA_SRC_SCK_1..4 format VTSData.ServerData.IPn:Portn directly (no longer trusts the caller's Sender for socket sources, since the caller had wrong indices); OTA_SRC_SMS uses the passed Sender (the real phone number) with a 'SMS' fallback only if empty; BLE/RS232/RS485 keep generic labels (spec's SOURCE examples don't define an address form for them). Separately fixed SendResponce()'s IP index bugs (SCK_2 now passes IP2, SCK_3 now passes IP3) and added the missing 'else if(IsServer==OTA_SRC_SCK_4)' branch so an SCK4-sourced legacy command no longer falls into the BLE branch and no longer triggers BLE_SendReply().
evidence: Same AMD3 PDF SOURCE-format requirement as the ParseStandardAIS140Command fix. Confirmed via full read of MakeParamChangeString (Server.c ~2410) and its only caller SendResponce (Server.c ~4103-4147) that IsServer==OTA_SRC_SCK_4 had no matching else-if and therefore fell into the final unconditional else (BLE_SendReply + MakeParamChangeString("BLE",...)).
verification: Full `Make.bat new_release` GCC build succeeded (GCC Compiling Finished Successfully) after both edits; no new warnings/errors introduced (the one pre-existing SystemRecovery_RequestReset implicit-declaration warning just shifted line number due to inserted lines). Behavioral/on-device verification NOT done - no hardware/live server available this session.
must_not_repeat: There were TWO independent producers of the $PVT OTAResp SOURCE field (ParseStandardAIS140Command for AMD3 '$'+IMEI frames, MakeParamChangeString/SendResponce for legacy 'SET:XXX' SMS-syntax commands) - both are now fixed and consistent. If a third command-entry path is ever added, check it also builds SOURCE the same way rather than inventing another hardcoded label.

evidence: Device received adc_value ~510; with /4095 scaling: (510/4095)*3.3*7.32 + 0.67 = 3.68V. Hardware.c line 861 sets IsMain=0 when MainsVolt <= 6.0V. PVT packet formatted MainsVolt as 3.6 and IsMain as 0.
guard: Do not define NUVOTON_M032 or use 12-bit ADC scaling for M031 boards; always verify ADC bit depth and MainsVolt threshold (>6.0V) when touching voltage conversion.
summary: Reverted NUVOTON_M032 macro and 12-bit ADC (/4095.0f) scaling in custom_feature_def.h, MCU.h, and MCU.c. The 12-bit divisor caused 10-bit M031 ADC values (~500 at 12V mains) to be scaled down to 3.68V. Because 3.68V is below the 6.0V threshold in Hardware.c (PeriPheralVal.MainsVolt > 6.0), PeriPheralVal.IsMain was set to 0 (power disconnected) while ignition remained 1, causing  packet to show '...,1,0,3.6,3.5,...' and GETVSTATUS SMS to show 'MV: 3.68'. Restored standard 10-bit scaling (/1023.0f).
title: Reverted Nuvoton M032 12-bit ADC scaling and restored M031 10-bit ADC scaling

summary: Replaced immediate ThreadSleep(6000) and hard Ql_Reset(0) in VRESET handling with QueueVResetResponse. Now properly populates LastOTAResponse with Mode=SET, CmdId=VRESET, Value=System Restarting, Status=1, Pending=1, AddAlert(CONF_CHANGE_ALERT), and sets AIS140ResetPending=2. This allows the server loop to transmit the OA,12 alert frame (,...,OA,12,L,...(SRC|SET|VRESET:System Restarting:1)) and confirm delivery before executing SystemRecovery_RequestReset(VRESET).

summary: Implemented FEATURE_GPS_LAST_FIX_FALLBACK in custom_feature_def.h, GPS.h, and GPS.c. When GPS is fixed, live values (Latitude, Longitude, Direction, Altitude, Speed, Heading, PDOP, HDOP, and string representations) are cached into LastFixedGPS. When GPS fix is lost, LastFixedGPS values are populated into active GPS fields and string buffers so packets to server and SMS status/location display the last known coordinates, while GPSFix accurately reports 0 (unfixed). When GPS re-acquires a fix, live data resumes immediately.
title: Store last fixed GPS data and fallback when unfixed
